abstract: Educational foundation models must do more than produce correct answers: they must understand where a problem sits in a curriculum, diagnose why a learner is struggling, and choose an appropriate instructional response. Existing educational language models often specialize in either subject problem solving or tutoring, while their training mixtures are commonly organized by source or task and do not explicitly balance these capabilities. We present OmniEdu, an open family of foundation models for K–12 learning and teaching, trained with a capability-oriented instruction-tuning corpus. The corpus combines more than 100 educational resources and general instruction sources and organizes supervision around four complementary capabilities: subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical action and scaffolding. A multi-stage pipeline performs deterministic cleaning, semantic auditing and rewriting, task-specific quality scoring, token-budgeted diversity selection, and pedagogical instruction assignment, yielding 69,999 examples and 15.96M supervised response tokens, including 60,951 education-specific examples. We fine-tune 4B, 9B, and 27B models and evaluate them on curriculum-grounding, K–12 problem-solving, and pedagogical-tutoring benchmarks, with auxiliary tests of general capability. Across model scales, education-oriented tuning consistently improves all three educational capability groups. In particular, OmniEdu-27B reaches 63.12% EM / 76.69% F1 on K12-Bench, 85.89% on MathFish, 86.95% on EDUMATH, 78.74% on MathTutorBench’s Scaffold setting, and the best Teaching average of 3.02 on LongTutor among the evaluated models. These results show that carefully curated, capability-balanced supervision can turn a general language model into a stronger educational system that not only solves problems, but also understands curriculum structure and supports effective teaching interactions.

sections.body: The introduction argues that answer accuracy alone does not measure educational usefulness. It proposes four capabilities: **subject competence**, **curriculum grounding**, **diagnostic reasoning**, and **pedagogical action and scaffolding**. It states that the education-specific pool of approximately 1.34M examples is reduced to 60,951 examples, and that the final mixture has 69,999 examples and 15.96M supervised response tokens. The stated gap is that existing educational models often specialize in either problem solving or tutoring, and these capabilities are often developed in separate systems or evaluated in isolation.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Educational models need problem solving, curriculum structure, diagnosis, and teaching, but these are often built and tested separately.

sections.body: This section groups related work into three areas. Open educational models include EduChat, MuduoLLM, and Confucius3-Math. Pedagogically oriented systems include LearnLM, ChatGPT Study Mode, and Khanmigo. The text says many frontier systems remain closed or rely on product-level orchestration, which makes their capabilities hard to reproduce. For data, it cites LIMA, AlpaGasus, Deita, and LESS on instruction-data quality and selection, and K12-KGraph and EDUMATH on curriculum-structured educational data. For evaluation, it groups benchmarks into learner competence, curriculum understanding, and pedagogical capability.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Related work spans open educational models, data-selection methods, and benchmarks, while many frontier tutoring systems remain closed.

sections.body:
The corpus is built in six stages, with provenance and audit metadata kept throughout:

- Deterministic cleaning and decontamination leave 870,711 education-specific examples.
- LLM-assisted auditing gives each example a 0–100 usability score and leaves 440,100 examples.
- Preliminary k-center greedy selection on BGE-M3 embeddings reduces overrepresented sources, then fine-grained 1–5 scoring leaves 121,318 examples.
- Token-budgeted diversity selection within task buckets leaves 60,951 examples and approximately 12.0M supervised response tokens.
- Each example receives one of 20 pedagogical system instructions. Adding 9,048 general-purpose examples gives 69,999 examples in total.
sections.heading: Data Preparation
sections.headline: A six-stage pipeline cleans, audits, scores, and selects 60,951 education examples, then adds general data and pedagogical instructions for 69,999 examples.

sections.body: Each base model is fine-tuned with LlamaFactory for 3 epochs and compared with its base model, open-weight educational baselines, and proprietary models. On K12-Bench, OmniEdu-27B reaches 63.12% EM and 76.69% F1, compared with 52.11% EM and 73.48% F1 for its base model. It scores 85.89% on MathFish and 86.95% on EDUMATH. On MathTutorBench, its Scaffold win rate is 78.74%, compared with 57.16% for its base model. On LongTutor, it has the best Teaching average of 3.02. The text states two limits: knowledge-state diagnosis remains comparatively challenging, with OmniEdu-27B at 54.04% accuracy, and frontier proprietary models keep an advantage on some exam-style evaluations.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Tuning improves each base model at all three scales across curriculum, problem-solving, and tutoring benchmarks.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the four capabilities and the multi-stage corpus pipeline. It reports consistent improvements across 4B, 9B, and 27B models. It says OmniEdu-27B remains competitive with frontier proprietary models on K–12 problem solving and substantially outperforms existing open-weight educational models. It also says the general instruction-following, reasoning, and multimodal evaluations quantify the broader effects of education-oriented specialization. The authors conclude that carefully curated, capability-balanced supervision is an effective path toward educational foundation models that understand curriculum structure and support teaching interactions.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion argues capability-balanced supervision yields educational models that go beyond problem solving.

sections.body: The appendix keeps the table structure of the main text. Table 4 gives K12-Bench results by Ground, Prereq, Neighbor, Evidence, and Locate subtasks. Table 5 gives MathFish results for positive and negative curriculum-alignment cases. Table 6 gives EDUMATH format pass, classifier GOOD, and MaC results. Tables 13, 14, and 15 give IFEval, GPQA, and MMMU-Pro results for base and tuned models. Table 16 gives the training configuration, which is full-parameter supervised fine-tuning with LLaMA-Factory, a maximum sequence length of 32,768, and ZeRO-3 in DeepSpeed.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists per-subtask curriculum and general-capability tables and the full training configuration.
